text:
ConocoPhillips dropped slightly today despite oil prices holding strong, after climbing nearly 13% over two weeks on the back of rising crude prices and Middle East tensions. The stock had surged to $146.51 yesterday when Brent crude topped $109 following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Aramco facilities, but gave back a small fraction of those gains today as the immediate headline momentum faded.

The broader picture supporting the stock remains intact: Brent crude is trading around $126 per barrel globally, and physical oil delivery costs have spiked sharply due to surging tanker rates — meaning refiners and producers are getting paid significantly more than the headline price suggests. Continued geopolitical risk from Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure keeps downside pressure on global supply, a tailwind for U.S. oil producers even if today's move was modest.
